Elena — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers below, and I attached a one-pager with the pricing shapes.

1) Staged activation: yes. AWS private offers can be issued with a single PO and then activated in stages. We typically set the private offer to the maximum commit and then allow the buyer to provision gradually; activation and seat counts are handled at purchase activation time. If you want the pilot to have different unit pricing, we usually do a two-line PO (pilot line + long-term line) with clear activation dates.

2) Term structure: flexible. We can do a 12m pilot that automatically rolls into a 36m commitment with a transition clause — or set a 36m PO where only year 1 is initially provisioned. Legal typically prefers a single PO with a defined activation window (e.g., 90 days to provision additional capacity) to avoid duplicate contract records.

3) Approvers: for the 450k/yr tier we usually see: procurement (procurement@...), BU head for budget approval, and CFO for any multi-year commitment over $250k. If they want to avoid CFO sign-off, we can propose an auto-proration clause for year 1 to keep contractual exposure lower.

Evidence: attaching SOC 2 summary and a 1-page activation checklist.

Next steps: if this approach works, I can draft a recommended private offer structure for AWS (two-line PO with pilot pricing + enterprise line, activation window 180 days) and loop in our marketplace team to prepare the DocuSign + AWS private offer link.

Cheers,
Olga
